name: NC-12
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Alma Adams seeking re-election with a large cash advantage
Republican challenger is minimally funded with no outside support
Prediction markets price the Democrat near certain to win
model.rationale: The D+24 district, Adams's incumbency, and her roughly 16-to-1 fundraising edge over a challenger with essentially no cash make this a Safe D race, and Polymarket prices her win probability at about 96%. No polls or expert ratings exist, but fundamentals alone leave little doubt.
model.watch: Any late outside spending or a polling surprise showing a much tighter race would be the main signal to revisit, though none is currently evident.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alma Adams, the Democratic incumbent in this Charlotte-area district, is running for re-election in a seat with a D+24 partisan lean. She has raised about $370,000 and holds roughly $457,000 in cash, while Republican Jack Codiga has raised under $29,000 and reports almost nothing on hand, with no outside spending on either side.

No general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals, which point strongly to the incumbent. Prediction markets also price Adams as an overwhelming favorite. The district's heavy Democratic tilt and the challenger's minimal resources make an upset highly unlikely.
